description: Add promise error handling in image load chain during PDF export. Image fetch failures currently cause unhandled promise rejections and incomplete PDFs. Wrap all image operations in try-catch and add .catch() handlers with graceful fallback (skip or use placeholder).
steps: Open src/services/export-engine.js and locate image embedding logic in generatePdf() method
Find all async image fetch/load operations (e.g., fetch(), Image.onload, Promise chains)
Wrap each in try-catch block with catch clause that logs warning and continues gracefully
Add .catch() handlers on all Promise chains related to image loading
On image load failure: skip the image with console.warn('Image failed: <path>') OR embed a 1x1 transparent GIF placeholder
Ensure no unhandled promise rejections remain in the export pipeline
Add a unit test that exports a document with a broken image reference and verifies no errors thrown
acceptance_criteria: Exporting a document with broken image references completes without console errors
No unhandled promise rejections in DevTools console during export
PDF is generated successfully even if images fail to load
Warning messages logged for each failed image (for debugging)
verification: Manual test: create .md with ![alt](broken.png), export as PDF, verify completion and no console errors
findings: Implementation complete: (1) Added try-catch error handling in generateStandaloneHtml() around image processing with console.warn logging for failed images; (2) Enhanced printHtmlDocument() with comprehensive .catch() handlers on all Promise chains (fonts.ready, image loading, math rendering, animation frames, print operations); (3) All image load failures now log warnings instead of throwing unhandled promise rejections; (4) Gracefully skips failed images or uses SVG fallback placeholders; (5) All 359 tests pass including 3 new test cases for broken image handling; (6) Verified no regressions across integration and unit test suites.
